Fibonacci EXTENSIONS (127%, 161.8%, named by R10-17) are the same arithmetic with the ratio above 1 -- reachable by moving fibRatio, so no second rule.

blocked.description: CANONICAL SWING-PIVOT PRIMITIVE for the whole corpus. The bar `strength` bars ago is a confirmed swing high: its high is at or above the highs of the `strength` bars on each side of it (mirror: swing low, its low at or below the lows of the `strength` bars each side). The pivot is known only `strength` bars after it prints, which is what makes it lookahead-safe. This is detection ONLY; retaining the pivot's price/bar for later comparison is the separate machinery every rule below needs.
blocked.pseudocode: high[strength] >= highest(high, strength)[0] && high[strength] >= highest(high, strength)[strength + 1]

complexity.reason: 2 x strength fixed-offset comparisons, or two Highest windows; no persistence, no scan-back

blocked.merge_notes: Nine independent restatements across all three volumes; the corpus's most-repeated primitive. TWO families were offered. (a) The one-bar fractal, confirmed one bar late, with AT-OR-ABOVE comparisons: R00-27/R00-28/V00-10, straight from Brooks's glossary ('Its high is at or above that of the bar before it and that of the bar after it'). (b) The N-bar strength pivot with STRICT comparisons and a scan-back for the k-th most recent pivot: T13-01, T14-01, T15-04, T15-05, T17-01, TP3-02, all defaulting strength = 2 and all graded 'hard'. WINNER: family (a)'s comparison sense (>=, Brooks's own words) with family (b)'s `strength` parameter, since (a) is exactly (b) at strength = 1 and one parameterized rule covers both. The 'hard' grade in family (b) belongs to the scan-back-and-remember step, not to detection: detection at a fixed `strength` is 2 x strength fixed-offset comparisons, so this rule is SIMPLE and priority A. Brooks never states a pivot strength (he reads swings visually); 2 is the reading five separate miners converged on for 5-minute charts, 3 appears in T03-04 and T07-47. TIE BEHAVIOUR: with >= a flat run of equal highs makes every bar in the run a swing high; the strict-> variant (family b) suppresses that but also misses Brooks's literal 'at or above'. Kept >= per the glossary; the authoring pass can expose the sense as a structural constant if flat ledges prove noisy (see Ledge, which is exactly that shape). ALL OTHER BUCKETS should name this key in depends_on_keys and write swingHigh(strength) / swingLow(strength) in pseudocode. SwingHigh/SwingLow have no register row yet; they are recorded as needed, which does not downgrade this rule.

blocked.merge_notes: Four statements of one bar test. blocked.merge_notes: T06-16 and R28-22 state the adjacent-bar form (gap 1); V00-26 and T10-08 state the one-bar-gap form (gap 2), so one rule with a `gap` parameter, default 1. T10-08 adds a V-shape conjunct (low[1] must be above both matching lows, so the pair is a real dip and not two bars of a slide) and a close-up conjunct; the close is bar_anatomy, but the V-shape is a genuine strengthening that only bites at gap >= 2 - recorded here for the authoring pass, which may want it as a second rule rather than as an input. blocked.merge_notes: Brooks's glossary ledge, restated three times, plus its entry (R28-23). TWO definitions: PAIRWISE over the window (R00-18, V00-25 - any two bars in the window match each other, O(n^2) and it can fire on a level price is nowhere near now) and ANCHORED at the current bar (T00-09 - count bars matching low[0]). WINNER: anchored, per the mechanizability rule: one pass, and it only fires while price is AT the ledge, which is what the entry needs. Tolerance 0 in R00-18/T00-09 ('identical lows'), 1 tick in V00-25; default 0, Brooks's literal word. R28-23 adds a limit order a tick or two above the ledge bottom - under the close-then-next-open convention that offset is not representable, so R28-23 collapses into this rule and its ledgeEntryTicks is recorded, not carried. Kept apart from MicroDoubleExtreme: at lookback 2 / minMatches 2 the two coincide, but in general this one accepts a match at any lag inside the window while MicroDoubleExtreme requires it at exactly `gap`.
